text_blocks.snippet: Prevent ice dams on Utah roofs by stopping warm attic air from melting snow on the roof. Seal warm air leaks, add attic insulation, and ensure proper roof ventilation. You can also use a roof rake for heavy snow or install low-power electric de-icing cables in gutters.
snippet_highlighted_words: stopping warm attic air from melting snow on the roof

text_blocks.snippet: Stop Heat Loss From Your Home

list.snippet: Seal bypasses: Close gaps around plumbing vents, chimneys, and attic hatches.

Add insulation:
Keep attic floor temperatures cold to match outdoor winter weather.
Improve airflow: Clear soffit and ridge vents so cold air moves freely under the roof deck.
Use a roof rake: Pull fresh snow off the lower roof edge from the safety of the ground.

Install heat cables:
Wrap constant-wattage heat tape along problem eaves and downspouts to maintain a drain path.
Apply calcium chloride: Fill a nylon sock with calcium chloride pellets and lay it across an active ice dam to melt a channel; avoid regular rock salt, which ruins roofing materials and plants.

references.title: Easy Heat Roof Gutter Cable ADKS
references.snippet: Keep your gutters and downspouts flowing all winter long! Prevent ice dam formation and the costly damage it can cause by installing the EasyHeat ADKS kit. Ice dams are frozen ridges of melting snow that stop the water from flowing off the roof. Ice dams can form on roofs, eaves, dormers, roof valleys, gutters, skylights and downspouts and can cause shingle damage, water leakage into the roof, damage to insulation, moisture leakage into walls and ceilings, and gutter or downspout problems. The ADKS de-icing cable is installed over the unheated portions of the roof above the overhang or into gutters or downspouts to create an ice-free pathway for melting water to drain. The ADKS cable plugs into a standard 120 VAC GFCI protected three-wire grounded outlet. Prevents dangerous icicles from building up over pathways and doors. Keeps gutters and down spouts open and clear for water to flow. The use of a temperature and moisture sensing control such as EasyHeat's RS-2 is highly recommended. It measures both temperature and moisture to turn the system on or off in response to changing weather conditions.
